sentences.text: The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed, by the petitioners/accused Nos.3, 4 and 6 seeking quashment of the proceedings against them in C.C.No.163 of 2021, on the file of the IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Vijayawada, for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A IPC and 3 & 4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: Heard Sri Shaik Md Umar Abdullah, learned counsel, representing Ms.Jyothi Ratna Anumolu,
learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri M.D.Abdul Majeed, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and Ms.K.Priyanka Lakshmi, Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that petitioners herein are A.3, A.4 and A.6.
A.3 is sister of A.1.
A.4 is the husband of A.3 and A.6 is alleged to have the objectionable intimacy with A.1.
Learned counsel further would submit that there are no specific allegations made against the petitioners except stating that A.1 had affair with A.6.
No specific incident as to the alleged harassment has been referred against A.3 and A.4 in the complaint which is of omnibus allegation.
Learned counsel further would submit that continuing criminal proceedings against the married sister and her spouse is mere abuse of process of law.

Learned counsel finally would submit that the case against A.6 for the offence punishable under Section 498-A IPC is not maintainable in the light of the judgment in Venkata Naga Malleswari Anamaripudi v. State of A.P. 1 and U. Suvetha v.
State2.
4.

entities.text: Venkata Naga Malleswari Anamaripudi v. State of A.P. 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 would submit that there are clear allegations against A.3 and A.4 in the complaint.
The case against A.6 is maintainable.
A.1 has been maintaining illegal relationship with A.6 even prior to the marriage as such she is also responsible for the harassment of A.1 towards his wife.

In support of his contention, learned counsel placed reliance on the judgment of a Co-ordinate Bench of High Court of Gujarath at Ahemdabad in Criminal Misc.
Application No.468 of 2010 dated 05.02.2014.
5.

entities.text: High Court of Gujarath at Ahemdabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor supported the version of respondent No.2.
6.
A perusal of the contents of the complaint and the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners reveal that A.6 is no way related to family of Respondent No.2.

This Court in Venkata Naga Malleswari Anamaripudi v. State of A.P., observed that Section 498-A of I.P.C. is a powerful weapon engrafted by the law, to the rescue of a married woman, subjected to cruelty or harassment by husband or by the relative of husband.

entities.text: Venkata Naga Malleswari Anamaripudi v. State of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, this Court having referred the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in U. Suvetha v. State, interpreted the term "relative" as appearing in Section 498A of I.P.C. to mean persons related by blood, marriage or adoption.
2023 SCC OnLine AP 4319 (2009) 3 SCC (Cri) 36 7.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and another3, highlighted the requirement of taking the realities into consideration and legislating, especially in the context of the Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

entities.text: Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant observations made in the context of the present case highlighting the duty of this Court, in the said judgment are as follows;
"25.

If a person is made to face a criminal trial on some general and sweeping allegations without bringing on record any specific instances of criminal conduct, it is nothing but abuse of the process of the court.

The court owes a duty to subject the allegations levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, prima facie,
whether there is any grain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving certain individuals in a criminal charge, more Janthika Naomi Ethel vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100076192/
2 particularly when a prosecution arises from a matrimonial dispute."

entities.text: Janthika Naomi Ethel vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (emphasis supplied)

8. In Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and others Vs. State of Bihar and others4, it was held by the Hon'ble Apex Court as follows:
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and others Vs. State of Bihar and others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against 2024 INSC 369 (2022) 6 SCC 599 the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.

22.Therefore, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of any specific role attributed to the accused appellants, it would be unjust if the Appellants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial, i.e., general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant's husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been highlighted by this court in varied instances, that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must therefore be discouraged."
6.

Considering the submissions made and a fair look at the contents of the complaint, as rightly put forth by the learned counsel for the petitioners, except for the omnibus and bald allegations against A.3 and A.4, no specific incidents are referred in the complaint.
The allegations would show that A.3 and A.4 engaged A.1 to harass his wife.
Admittedly, A.3 is the married sister and A.4 is her husband.
It is not the case of the complainant that they are staying with A.1 and respondent No.2 under the same roof.

Coming to the case of A.6, a cursory look at the judgment relied upon by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 shows that the learned judge distinguished the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in U. Suvetha Vs. State by Inspector of Police & another, and opined that there are no allegations that the girlfriend of the husband abetted the husband of the complainant in harassing her.

entities.text: U. Suvetha Vs. State by Inspector of Police & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in the case before the High Court of Gujarat, the girlfriend of the husband could be treated as an abettor to harass the wife so as to commit the offence under Section 498-A of IPC, falling under the ambit of the word "relative."
The case referred to above is not helpful to the case of respondent No.2 in the present set of facts.
There is no iota of evidence against A.6 to suggest that she abetted A.1 in committing an offence under Section 498-A of IPC.
It appears that A.6 is a married woman.
In light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in U. Suvetha Vs. State, the case against A.6 is not maintainable.
In view of the aforementioned premises, the petition is liable to be allowed.
7. In the result, this Criminal Petition is allowed.
The case against the petitioners is hereby quashed.
